subject: Medisync: recommended models, benchmarks, and JSON-schema hardening
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
To: Claire Johnson <claire@medisync.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 01 Nov 2028 15:10:00 -0800
Subject: Medisync discovery — recommended models, bench links, and next steps

Thanks again for the productive call this morning, Claire — appreciated the context on clinical note normalization and the low-tolerance for hallucination in the downstream EHR ingestion path. Recap and concrete next steps below so we have a single action plan.

Quick recap (one-liner): Medisync will run a small benchmark on a ~10k example prompt set representative of production (structured fields + free-form clinician notes) to validate model accuracy, JSON-schema compliance, and retry behaviour for transient failures.

Recommended model candidates (based on today’s latency/throughput and accuracy constraints):
- redwood-instruct-medium-quant (8-bit q8_0) — good latency, lower cost; strong on extraction tasks with tight schema constraints.
- llama3-8b-finetuned-structured — better factual consistency on clinical terminology; higher token cost but fewer hallucinations in our tests.
- fallbacks: redwood-instruct-small + aggressive schema enforcement for ultra-low-cost routing.

Bench & artifacts I’m attaching / linking:
- Attached: Medisync_MVP_prompt_set_v1.csv (10k prompts, anonymized)
- Attached: Medisync_benchmark_spec_v1.md (metrics, SLOs, run instructions)
- Drive: prompt set + results sheet: https://drive.redwood/research/medisync/benchmarks#sheet
- JSON schema draft for output object (link to gist): https://gist.github.com/redwood/medisync-json-schema-v1

Key evaluation axes we’ll run:
1) Schema compliance rate (strict JSON Schema v2020-12)
2) Semantic correctness for extracted fields (precision/recall on key clinical fields)
3) Regression detection (baseline vs candidate model; automate alerts on token-level hallucination spikes)
4) Retry robustness: idempotent retries, backoff behaviour, and KV-cache effects on stateful calls

Asks from Medisync for the bench to proceed:
- Final confirmation that the attached prompt set is safe to use (PII/anonymization OK)
- A sample of the real production schema edge-cases (long notes, embedded lists) if available
- A short window to test with your procurement contact for short-term trial terms

Proposed mutual action plan (MAP):
- Wed 11/1: share prompt set & bench spec (done)
- Thu 11/2: Redwood SE runs model candidate bench and posts initial results in the Drive sheet; we’ll also run structured-output schema conformance tests with the harness linked in the gist
- Fri 11/3: 30-min sync to review results and agree on a canary config (region, batching, cache TTL)

Next steps for you: confirm prompt set usage and loop in procurement if they want trial usage terms; copy procurement to this thread when ready.

Attachments: Medisync_MVP_prompt_set_v1.csv (CSV, 10k rows), Medisync_benchmark_spec_v1.md (MD)

Cheers,
Naomi Feldman
Account Exec | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Medisync discovery — recommended models, bench links, and next steps

Thanks Naomi — this is very clear, and the plan sounds good. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Prompt set: we’ve run a quick internal check; the anonymization looks fine. I did mark ~120 rows with embedded HL7 snippets — I can extract those into a separate file if you prefer to run them as an edge-case subset.
- Schema: the gist looks like it covers our immediate fields; however we have one complex field ("medication_list") that can be a nested array or a string blob depending on the clinician. How strict do you need the upstream to be for that field?
- Procurement: looping in procurement; they’ll confirm trial license terms and whether we need an NDA amendment for the trial tokens.

We’re happy to proceed with the attached prompt set + an edge-case subset of the HL7 rows. Please proceed with your bench run.

Claire

Hey team — forwarding Medisync confirmation. Ben, can you run the initial bench on the three candidate variants (redwood-instruct-medium-quant, llama3-8b-finetuned-structured, redwood-instruct-small) and populate the Drive sheet by EOD? Focus on: schema compliance (use the gist schema), hallucination signals (we’ll use the bench spec thresholds), and retry handling.

Bench specifics / test harness notes: 
- Use the harness in the gist to validate schema conformance per-response. Failures should include the full response and the schema validation error.
- For retries, simulate transient 500s and run idempotent retries with exponential backoff; measure duplicate/non-idempotent outputs.
- Run one pass with KV cache warm to observe token savings and potential state leakage into subsequent extractions.

Marissa — please prepare a 30-min review slot for Friday with Claire. I’ll bring the canary config recs (batch sizes, cache TTLs, quantization profile).

Attachments: Medisync_benchmark_spec_v1.md (MD)

Thanks —
Naomi
